_readme: The formats bank. These are BUILT formats -- a sequence picks one by name,
it never invents a layout. Adding an entry here is how the bank grows, and
nothing writes a slide design that is not in it.
The rule is the hooks bank's rule, for the same reason: a format that has
been rendered, looked at and corrected is worth more than a better idea
nobody has seen. `pipeline/slides.py` refuses a `format` that is not here.
name    what goes in a slides.json `format`. Must exist in
what    one line. What is actually on the slide.
needs   the slide keys this format reads. A format renders without them,
it just renders less -- except where marked required.
ground  what sits behind the type: a photo, a texture, a flat colour, or
nothing. One per sequence, never mixed.
good_for  when to reach for it. Scored by eye, not by a matcher --
fourteen entries is a list you read, not a search problem.
from    the reference it was read off, or 'improvised' where there was
none. Improvised is not a lesser class; it means the reference
set had no example and the gap was the reason to build it.
sample  the folder that renders one, under stories/. More than one where a format has a variant worth looking at separately.

formats.name: textured
formats.what: Centred: a terracotta pill, an extra-bold headline, a semibold paragraph with one clause in the same terracotta, and a screenshot on a light card below.
good_for: a numbered walkthrough
six slides that must read as one document
when you have a brand texture
formats.note: Its words are bounded by the card: about three lines of body. slides.py counts them and refuses more.

formats.name: blurred
formats.what: The cover photo blurred behind every slide, a light card in the upper half, a ghosted italic step number behind a tight headline, paragraph in regular weight.
good_for: showing a UI
a student with a good photo and no brand assets
a set that must read as one piece
formats.note: The first slide of a set usually names no image: there is nothing to show yet, so it carries no card.

formats.name: labels
formats.what: The photograph untouched, no scrim, and the text small in the app's own black label boxes, each line its own box.
good_for: a personal day
a reply to something
anything that should look typed rather than designed
formats.note: No handle, no dots, no logo. The app draws none, and adding them is the tell.

formats.name: stack
formats.what: A weight ladder over a dim photo: tight bold headline, a light-weight list, then a bold payoff with one accent word underlined.
good_for: far more text than a still normally carries
an argument in three tiers
a list that adds up to a number
formats.note: Put a | in `emphasis` before the words that take the accent and the underline.

formats.name: titled
formats.what: A sharp photograph and a title set as four different cuts -- bold, bold italic, serif, bracketed italic -- over two angled overlapping cards.
good_for: the cover of a carousel
a title that has to carry four separate ideas
formats.from: Comment GUIDE and I'll send it.jpg
formats.note: The ladder is headline, kicker, emphasis, body -- in that order down the slide, not in importance order. Give `steps` and it sets them as live text in a terminal card, centred: commands are typed, so they are set rather than photographed and stay sharp at any size. Two screenshots scatter at angles; ONE sits straight and contained, and the card takes its height from it. On a story it draws a next-arrow instead of the dots, which are a carousel's affordance.

formats.name: beforeafter
formats.what: An italic line, a huge accent number, a parenthetical, two screenshots down the right, and a long arrow between the two dates on the left.
good_for: one number that changed
a claim that needs two screenshots to be believed
formats.note: `emphasis` is the two dates separated by a slash: 'FÖRE/EFTER'. Give `steps` instead and it draws that sequence down the middle with an arrow between each, in place of the cards -- for a claim whose subject is the order and which has nothing to photograph. Omit `handle` and the footer goes with it.

formats.name: collage
formats.what: Portrait screenshots at three sizes, overlapping, over a blurred photo, with green chips over the figures and white caption boxes carrying black text.
good_for: proof
several results at once
a DM or dashboard worth showing
formats.note: The chip is the format. Each names its own x and y as a fraction of the frame, placed by hand -- only whoever took the screenshot knows where the number is. Three places, filled in order.

formats.name: ticker
formats.what: One figure sized to fill the frame and clip when it is longer, a mono label above and a line below.
formats.ground: none, a blurred photo, or a texture -- each under a vignette
good_for: a single number that is the whole point
an opener
a closer
formats.note: `image` is a photograph and is darkened; `background` is a texture and is not.

formats.name: thread
formats.what: The conversation drawn rather than screenshotted: bubbles over a blurred photo, the sender's name blurred.
good_for: a reaction worth reading
something someone said about the work
formats.note: Drawn, so it is not evidence -- for a thread worth reading, not a thread worth proving. The name is always blurred: a real thread has a real person in it.
